## Exact constructed stopping control

Run `python3 emmy/stopping_control.py`; saved output is emmy/stopping_control.json. No molecular integrals or hardware simulation enter this calculation.

Consider independent logical two-level modes with

\[h=\begin{pmatrix}0&v\\v&\Delta\end{pmatrix},\qquad
v^2=d(\Delta+d),\qquad H=\sum_{j=1}^{m}h_j.\]

Each mode has exact ground energy \(-d\). Take \(m=100\), \(\Delta=1\) Hartree and \(d=5\times10^{-6}\) Hartree. Initialise all modes in their reference configuration and let each pool operator rotate an individual mode. This is a generic ADAPT-QSCI-style logical-mode construction, not P's molecular pool. A two-state logical subspace can be encoded in fixed-particle configurations; no claim of realistic dispersion integrals follows.

An exact first-mode update changes selected energy by \(d\), below P's stated threshold. The remaining error is

\[(m-1)d=0.000495\ \mathrm{Ha}=0.310617\ \mathrm{kcal/mol}.\]

This conclusion assumes the literal earliest consecutive-energy stopping rule with no minimum iteration count. It does not show premature convergence in P's molecular runs. A finite warm-up postpones the construction; it cannot turn energy increments alone into a general error bound.

The newly rotated mode has excited-state probability

\[p=\frac{d}{\Delta+2d}=4.99995\times10^{-6}.\]

With \(N_s=100000\), its probability of never being seen is \((1-p)^{N_s}=0.606533\). If seen, the energy change is below threshold; if unseen, it is zero. Both branches pass the literal energy-change check while other modes remain absent.
sources.where: A separate stopping construction requires many similar small gains and stopping at the earliest qualifying iteration; adding initial iterations exempt from stopping changes it.
